findings.title: Compilation error: isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() called without required argument
findings.body: The change introduces a call `!isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with no arguments in `UsernameForm.authenticate`. The only available method in the inheritance chain is `UsernamePasswordForm.isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)`, which requires a `UserModel` argument. There is no zero-argument overload, so this code will not compile and the entire services module will fail to build. The intended call is almost certainly `!isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())` (or, more defensively, guarding against a null user). Without this fix, none of the new UsernameForm re-authentication tests (e.g. `PasskeysUsernameFormTest.webauthnLoginWithDiscoverableKey_reauthentication`) can be executed.

findings.title: shouldDisplayAuthenticators not overridden alongside shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators
findings.body: The new `shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators` override in `WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator` returns `false`, ensuring no authenticators bean is set on the form. However, the related hook `shouldDisplayAuthenticators(AuthenticationFlowContext)` in the parent `WebAuthnAuthenticator` (line ~147) still returns `context.getUser() != null` and is not overridden here. During a re-authentication with `context.getUser() != null`, `fillContextForm` therefore sets `WebAuthnConstants.SHOULD_DISPLAY_AUTHENTICATORS=true` while `WebAuthnAuthenticatorsBean` is null. The login template can render an empty authenticator section or otherwise leak inconsistent UI state. `shouldDisplayAuthenticators` must also return `false` here for the conditional UI path to be consistent with the 'Do not show authenticators during login with conditional passkeys' intent stated in the comment.

findings.title: NoSuchElementException import is now unused
findings.body: The diff replaces `Assert.assertThrows(NoSuchElementException.class, () -> driver.findElement(By.xpath("//form[@id='webauth']")))` with a positive `Matchers.notNullValue()` assertion, so the `org.openqa.selenium.NoSuchElementException` import is no longer referenced. Leaving the unused import can fail strict unused-import checks and adds noise; it should be removed in the same commit.
